shared_pass_resolution.signatures: _Plain.__init__(tables=False, blocks=False, images=False); normalize(body, era, tables=False, blocks=False, images=False) -> (text, tables, blocks, images); select_and_normalize(raw, tables=False, blocks=False, images=False) -> (text, meta, warnings, tables, blocks, images). `blocks` keeps the positional slot S9 gave it so their call sites did not move; `images` is appended.
decisions: ONE _tidy mark map for all three annotations. Both sides built their own `olds` set; merged, table marks, block marks and image marks go into a single sorted set rewritten in one pass. This is the decision that keeps 'the text is identical whatever is asked for' true by construction rather than by three separate careful implementations — and it is why the byte-identity result below is meaningful.

The branch stays INSIDE handle_starttag's if/elif chain rather than becoming a standalone statement like S9's bold tracking. Load-bearing: `elif self.skip_depth: pass` is the second branch, so keeping ours in the chain is what preserves 'an inside /ix:header/ix:hidden is never recorded' (INV-S5), which normalize.py::_demo pins. S9's bold `if` is a separate statement after the chain and must run for every tag including img, so both forms coexist.
self.tables = [] if (tables or blocks) else None — S9's rule, kept, because blocks imply tables. self.images is independent.

The early return `if not tables` became `if not (tables or images)`, so an images-only call still takes the marks path; _place_tables is now guarded by `if tables:` because p.tables is None on an images-only call and S9's unconditional call would have crashed there.
txt era returns (text, [] if tables, pre-block if blocks, [] if images) — both sides' answers, unchanged.
